- **When to use:** When geometry accuracy is prioritized over pure photometric fidelity, or when shape-radiance ambiguity leads to false geometry [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that common ray-based losses (like photometric loss) have low sensitivity to false geometry due to shape-radiance ambiguity. It further explains that the CF loss focuses significantly more on geometric errors and can be used to improve geometry. The text also notes that increasing the weight factor or number of rays relieves issues like 'thick surface' (geometry errors), but warns that if the weight is too large, the color field cannot be well optimized (reducing photometric fidelity/PSNR). This directly supports the claim that CF loss is prioritized when geometry accuracy is more important than pure photometric fidelity, especially in cases of shape-radiance ambiguity.
